newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges up, Russian cracked strong.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges up, Russian cracked strong.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges ended higher on Thursday on good bunker demand and higher swaps, and cargoes were talked steady to a touch firmer, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded between $96 and $97 fob ARA compared with Wedenesday's highest deal at $96.25. Front month swaps were up 50 cents to $1, reflecting low prompt avails, traders said.
Most of the buying at the higher numbers was done by a major that has cut its fuel oil production since the start of the year.

"The market is stronger and this is a reflection of continuous good bunker demand, again today it was up at about 30,000 tonnes. The market is also firmer on firmness everywhere, Singapore, New York," a trader said.
High sulphur fuel cargoes were steady to a touch firmer on the cracked front, with Russian material talked in the $92/$95 mark, traders said.
"I've had two offers today, one at $94 for a high water content cargo and the other at $95," one trader said.
Traders said that some of the Russian straight-run cargoes may actually end in the cracked market with low buying interest from refiners for feedstock.
Supplies of non-Russian were low, with only one trader said to be offering cracked fuel at about $85 fob, or unchanged.
Low sulphur barges were quiet but offers were stronger by $1 with some sellers reaching $99, but little bidding was seen.
"The buyers should be around $97. When they want to buy they have pay levels above high sulphur (barges)," one broker said.
One percent continued quiet with the only buying interest heard from traders seeking to cover short positions. In the absence of deals, levels were put around $95/$97 on a fob basis.
"Low sulphur barges have moved up, albeit notionally, but cargoes have not. There's very little activity in the market and a lot of people are on holiday and there's little offers," one trader said.
